text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Islamist-led coalition rocked by Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's avoidance of criticism of Iran on infiltration by Kurdish rebels across Iranian border into Turkey.
- The pro-United States Iraqi Kurds started coming to Turkey after Baghdad-backed Kurdistan Democratic Party forces overtook rival Kurdish stronghold Arbil.
- Foreign minister Tansu Ciller voiced harsh criticism to her Iranian counterpart in his visit to Turkey, on the support Iran is said to give to separatist PKK.
- The Turkish security court in Ankara last year took a secret order to bug mobile telephones.
- Chamber of agriculturalists warns against the diminishing of agricultural land in Turkey.
- Islamist-led government to unveil its second economic package on Monday since taking office in June.
- Narcotics squad posts officers to 136 high schools in Istanbul to combat rising drug consumption.
- The new education year starts on Monday, with 14,363,595 students and 532,093 teachers set fill the classrooms.
